result.summary: Fixes RPC request handling when a malformed request specifies JSON-RPC version 2.0. Instead of returning an HTTP 400 error, the RPC server now returns HTTP 200 OK with the JSON-RPC error payload as required by the specification, avoiding an assertion failure in debug builds.
result.problem: Malformed requests that explicitly specify JSON-RPC 2.0 are misidentified as having an unparsed version, returning an HTTP error. In debug builds with authenticated RPC access, this incorrect assumption trips an assertion failure in JSONErrorReply and crashes bitcoind.
evidence: Author description notes an assertion failure in debug builds: httprpc.cpp:46 UniValue JSONErrorReply(UniValue, const JSONRPCRequest &, HTTPStatusCode &): 'jreq.m_json_version != JSONRPCVersion::V2' check failed.
Author notes release builds improperly return HTTP 400 alongside a JSON-RPC 2.0 error body instead of the standard HTTP 200.
result.scope_notes: Small patch (+26/-1) touching HTTP RPC request handling and an interface test.
result.card: This PR corrects HTTP status handling for malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 requests, returning HTTP 200 with an error object rather than HTTP 400. Currently, authenticated malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 requests cause an assertion failure and crash nodes compiled in debug mode. In release builds, it resolves non-compliant HTTP status codes when responding to malformed 2.0 requests.

risk.why: A mistake in HTTP status or RPC error formatting could break clients relying on strict HTTP error handling or JSON-RPC 2.0 compliance.
